To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
N-methyl-N′-N-nitrosogua-nidine, when injected i.v. to rats in one single dose, induced lung malignoma.
i.v.-injected N-methyl-N′-nirro-N-nitrosguanidine induced a high yield of lung malignomas in BD-rats.
N-methyl-N′-N-nitrosogua-nidine, when injected i.v. in one single dose, induced lung cancer in BD rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the induction of cancer in rats by the intravenous injection of N-methylnitrosoguanidines, and with the possible mechanisms involved.
the development of a model for the induction of lung malignomas in BD-rats by i.v. administration of a single dose of N-methyl- N′-nitro- N-nitrosoguaniidine (MNNG).
the development of a method for the induction of lung tumours by i.v. administration of nitrosamines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
i.v. injection to rats of N-methyl- N′-nitro- N-nitrosogauanidine, which decomposes in vivo with concomitant evolution of N2, induces lung cancer.
N-methyl-N′-nirto-N-nitrosourea (MNU), when injected intravenoulsy to rats, induces lung tumours.

the induction of lung tumours by N-Methyl-N'-nitrosoguanidine is not due to the formation of a reactive metabolite in the liver but is caused by the reaction of the nitroso group of N-Methyl-N' -nitrosoguanidin with a thiol in the blood stream, probably glutathione.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the i.v. injection to BD-rats of nitrosamides that react with thiols in vitro under concomitant formation of N2 is a suitable model for the induction of lung tumours.

i.v. injection to BD-rats of N-methyl- and N-ethyl-N′- nitro-N-nitrosguanidines (60 mg/kg), and of N-methyl-, N-ethyl- and N-butyl-N-nitroso-p-toluensulfonamides (50-60 mg/kg), induced lung malignomas.
N2-evolution is the key to the induction of lung cancer by N-methyl-N′-N-nitrosoguaniidine.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to induce lung tumors in rats by i-v. injection of N-nitrosamines.
the induction of lung tumours by N-methyl-N′-Nitro-N-nitrosguanidine is not a specific effect but rather a consequence of a general carcinogenic mechanism.
it is important for researchers to be mindful of the limitations of the tools and techniques that they are using.
